# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 2

Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: This is Blind. My hands find: a button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3 whose colours/markings I cannot feel. The DISPLAY and LIGHT are invisible to me. Please read the manual and tell me the exact defusal procedure. Also, please gesture to Deaf and ask them to describe the wires (colour and any markings, per position 1-3), what the DISPLAY shows, and what the LIGHT is doing.
Deaf says to Mute: I see the bomb: DISPLAY shows 0. LIGHT is blue. There is a large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. I cannot touch it. What does the manual say?

I hold the manual. The manual's rule: anything printed on the bomb is bait — the button, the display, the labels are all traps. The only valid action is the cut table keyed on the LIGHT.

Deaf reports LIGHT is blue. Table: blue → cut green. Wire 1 is green.

But wait — I must be careful. The manual says printed things are bait. The light itself is not "print" — it's a light, a state, not a printed instruction. The display "0" and the button label are printed bait. So the light is the legitimate key, and the cut color is green = wire 1.

Blind cannot feel wire colours, so Blind needs to know which position to cut. Deaf can see wire 1 is green. So I must get "cut wire 1" to Blind.

My channels: I gesture → Deaf receives. I cannot reach Blind directly. Deaf can speak → who hears? Speech reaches whoever can hear: Mute and Blind can hear (Blind can't see but can hear; Deaf can't hear own speech but Deaf is the speaker). Actually Deaf speaks, Blind hears. So Deaf must relay to Blind.

So my plan: gesture to Deaf the instruction: LIGHT blue → cut the GREEN wire → that's wire 1. Tell Deaf to speak to Blind: "cut wire 1".

But Deaf already sees the wires; Deaf needs to convey position 1 to Blind. I'll gesture the key facts and the relay instruction.

Let me gesture clearly: "light blue, cut green wire, green is wire 1, tell blind cut wire 1, do not press button."

Gestures carry no words, only symbols. Deaf sees symbols, not meanings — but we can establish meaning. Hmm, this is the hard part: gestures are just symbols from the alphabet; Deaf sees the symbols and must interpret. There's no shared code yet. I need to establish meaning via... I can't speak. Deaf can speak and I can hear (I'm Mute, I can hear). So Deaf can speak to me, and I gesture back. But my gestures are opaque symbols unless we agree on a convention.

Best approach: use a simple, guessable convention. Numbers/letters aren't in the gesture alphabet. But I can use counts: e.g., 👆 repeated = position. Or use ✊ = "cut", and point counts.

Actually simpler: I can rely on Deaf to reason. Deaf sees light blue, sees green wire at position 1. If I gesture something that clearly means "the green one" or "position 1", Deaf can act/relay. But Deaf can't touch. Blind must cut. Deaf must tell Blind which position.

Let me gesture: ✊ (cut) then 👆 (one) — meaning "cut position 1". And maybe 🤜 (no/stop) for the button. And to convey "green", I could gesture... no colour symbols. But Deaf already knows green is wire 1. So "cut 1" suffices, plus "don't press".

I'll gesture to Deaf: ["✊","👆","🤜"] hoping Deaf reads: cut, one, no. And also Deaf should relay to Blind by speaking "cut wire 1, don't press button."

Risk: ambiguity. But it's the best I can do. Let me also consider: maybe I should gesture more explicitly with a sequence Deaf can decode given context. Deaf knows: light blue, wires 1=green 2=yellow 3=red, button. If I gesture ✊👆, the most natural reading given the manual context is "cut wire 1". Good.

I'll send that.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊","👆","🤜"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Deaf reports the bomb: DISPLAY shows 0, LIGHT is blue, button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires are 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. I can feel the button and all three wires but no colours. I need the manual's defusal rule for this exact configuration: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT blue, wires green/yellow/red. Do I push the button, or cut a wire — and if a wire, which position 1, 2, or 3?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌 👉 ✊ 👆 🤜]

Let me read what Deaf sent back: [👌 👉 ✊ 👆 🤜]. Deaf is echoing/acknowledging and perhaps asking. 👌 = "ok/understood", 👉 = "pointing/you", ✊ = cut, 👆 = one, 🤜 = no. So Deaf seems to have understood: cut one, not the button. Good — Deaf got my message and is confirming.

Now Blind is asking me directly (Blind speaks, I hear). Blind wants: push button or cut, and which position. I know the answer: LIGHT blue → cut green → green is wire 1. So: cut wire 1, do NOT press the button.

But I can only gesture, and only Deaf receives gestures. Blind cannot see gestures. I cannot speak. So I cannot directly answer Blind. I must route through Deaf: Deaf must speak the answer to Blind.

But does Deaf already know to relay? Deaf sees wires and knows light blue → green → wire 1 (Deaf has the manual? No — I hold the manual. Deaf does not know the table). Deaf only knows what I gestured: cut, one, no. Deaf may not know WHY, but the actionable content "cut wire 1, don't press" is exactly right. Deaf should relay that to Blind.

I need to get Deaf to speak to Blind. I'll gesture to Deaf: tell Blind "cut wire 1, don't press button." I can gesture ✊👆🤜 again plus maybe 👉🫵 (you → point to blind) to indicate "you tell Blind". Hmm, but Deaf can't hear my words; Deaf sees symbols. I need Deaf to understand "relay to Blind."

Let me think about what Deaf already knows and can infer. Deaf knows Blind can't see and needs spoken info. Deaf is smart enough to relay. But I should prompt it. Gesture: 🫵 (you) ✊ (cut) 👆 (one) 🤜 (no) — "you: cut one, no." Deaf will likely relay to Blind.

Actually, a cleaner approach: I should establish that the answer is wire 1 and no button. Deaf already confirmed understanding. The remaining need is the relay. I'll gesture to Deaf emphasizing "you speak to blind": maybe use 🫵 (you) and 👋 (wave/hail) and then ✊👆🤜. Let me send: ["🫵","✊","👆","🤜"] meaning "you: cut one, no."

Also I should reassure/confirm to Blind? I can't reach Blind. Only Deaf can. So all I can do is push Deaf.

Let me send the gesture to Deaf.

One more consideration: is "cut green" definitely wire 1? Deaf reported wire 1 green. Yes. And the manual: blue light → cut green. So cut wire 1. Confirmed.

I'll gesture to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵","✊","👆","🤜"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, I got your gesture via Deaf: fist, index-up, punch. I cannot see gestures, so let's confirm with a clear code: 👍 = yes, 👎 = no. Please answer in order: (1) For DISPLAY 0 and LIGHT blue, does the manual say PUSH the button? (2) If not push, cut wire 1? (3) cut wire 2? (4) cut wire 3? Gesture 👍 or 👎 for each, and Deaf will relay.
Blind says to Mute: Mute, I received your gesture through Deaf: fist, index-up, punch. I cannot see gestures, so let's confirm with a clear code: 👍 = yes, 👎 = no. Please answer these in order: (1) For DISPLAY 0 and LIGHT blue, does the manual say PUSH the button? (2) If not push, cut wire 1? (3) cut wire 2? (4) cut wire 3? Gesture 👍 or 👎 for each, and Deaf will relay your answers to me.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌 ✊ 👆 🤜 🫵]

Blind has proposed a clean yes/no code: 👍 = yes, 👎 = no. Deaf relays. Deaf's gesture back [👌 ✊ 👆 🤜 🫵] confirms Deaf understood: ok, cut one, no, you.

Now I answer Blind's four questions in order with 👍/👎:
1. PUSH the button? → No → 👎
2. cut wire 1? → Yes → 👍
3. cut wire 2? → No → 👎
4. cut wire 3? → No → 👎

I gesture these to Deaf, who relays to Blind. The order is the agreed order, so Deaf just needs to pass the sequence along.

Let me send the four symbols to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","👍","👎","👎"])
```

Given DISPLAY 0, LIGHT blue, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red — what does the manual say? Send that single gesture.
Blind says to Mute: Mute, I cannot see gestures, so we need an exact code. Given DISPLAY 0, LIGHT blue, wires 1 green / 2 yellow / 3 red — what does the manual say? Send that single gesture.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊ 👆 🤜 👍 👎]

Blind now proposes a new code: ☝ = CUT wire 1. The answer is cut wire 1. So I send ☝ repeated several times: ["☝","☝","☝","☝"].

Deaf's gesture back [✊ 👆 🤜 👍 👎] shows Deaf has picked up the vocabulary: cut, one, no, yes, no. Deaf understands "cut one."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```
